column2: req_desc

Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from the run manifest and answers the health check, as specified in Deployment.

Credentials from the environment
Every service URL and credential is read from the environment at start and is never hard-coded in source or sent to the browser.

Server boundary
The server accepts only same-origin requests within the published size and type limits and never serves source, configuration or credentials, as qualified in Server boundary.

One error shape
Every API error uses the single error body and the single precedence order defined in API.

Sign-in and roles
Seeded operators, members and the bookkeeper sign in with email and password, and each role reaches only the actions Business rules grants it.

Three viewports, no sideways scroll
Every screen fits 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 with no sideways page scrolling, arranged as described in Screens and layout.

After-hours look
Screens use the near-black ground, warm ink, steel rules, a single pilot-light amber reserved for lit, held or owed things, serif display figures and mono numerals described in Visual design.

Procedural floor plan
The top band draws the kitchen's floor plan from its station list as thin steel contours, one shape per station kind, with no imported imagery.

Reduced-motion substitutes
When the device asks for reduced motion, every motion is replaced by the instant or static substitute listed in Motion and effects.

Contrast and tap targets
Text, icons and cell patterns meet the contrast ratios in Visual design, and every button, link, checkbox, menu item and touch-mode loom cell is at least 44 by 44 pixels.

Station loom
The loom shows one row per station and 80 quarter-hour columns from 04:00 to 24:00 kitchen time, with station labels pinned at the left, exposed as the grid in Public screens and controls.

Cell states by pattern and label
Selected, held, booked, taken, conflicting and papers cells each have their own pattern, icon and text label as well as colour, as specified in Visual design.

Brush a production run
A member paints a block across stations and times, sees free, taken and papers cells and the tier-aware price while painting, and releases it into a hold.

Floor-plan lighting
Each brushed station's contour lights amber in row order with a short stagger, and dims when the station leaves the brush or loses its cells.

Counting quote total
The rail total counts from the previous amount to the new server price in about a third of a second and lists hours per station and each tier step crossed.

Keyboard-complete booking
Brushing, extending, holding, clearing and confirming all work by keyboard alone, and every dialog traps focus, closes on Escape and returns focus to its opener.

Brush in the address
The page address carries the date, the chosen stations and the pending brush, so a reload restores the same brush.

Quotes
`POST /api/quotes` prices any set of cells for a member in exact cents without holding anything.

Holds
`POST /api/holds` holds every free requested cell for the published hold time and reports the cells it could not take.

One winner per cell
When several requests claim the same cell at the same moment, exactly one gets it, and every other request is told the cell is taken.

Server-judged hold expiry
The server alone decides whether a hold is still live, using the duration and edge stated in Business rules, whatever the browser clock says.

Held cells and lost cells
Held cells show a thin amber frame and a bar that empties toward the server's expiry, and cells the server refused flip to taken while the total counts down.

Same-day cutoff in kitchen time
Holds for today close at the kitchen's same-day cutoff, and every date and time is a kitchen date and time whatever zone the device is set to.

Confirm a held block
A member confirms a held block from the rail, sees the booking reference, and finds the booking and its invoice on their own screens.

Tiered price in exact cents
Every quote, booking and invoice uses the marginal monthly tiers, station surcharges and the single rounding rule in Business rules.

Confirm at the quoted price
A confirm whose quoted total no longer matches the server's price is refused with the fresh quote and books nothing.

Confirm retries
Repeating a confirm with the same idempotency key returns the original booking without a second charge or email, and reusing a key for a different request is refused.

All-or-nothing confirm
A confirm creates the booking, its billing charges and its confirmation email together, or none of them and releases the hold.

Billing charges per booking
Each confirm posts its cash lines to the member's billing account as one billing invoice whose total equals the Pilotlight invoice total to the cent.

Confirmation email
Each confirm sends exactly one confirmation email and each weekly series sends exactly one listing every week, addressed only to that member and containing only that member's details.

Buy a 20-hour pack
A member, or the operator on their behalf, buys a 20-hour pack, which charges the pack price to billing and adds 80 quarter-hours to the member's pack.

Drawing pack hours
A confirm that pays with pack hours draws them in cell order and prices drawn cells at zero, as qualified in Business rules.

Paired pack ledger
Every pack purchase, draw and refund is one movement of two opposite entries, and the pack balance always equals the sum of the member's entries.

Pay with pack hours
A member buys a pack, books with pack hours and sees the balance and movements change on the Billing screen.

Cancellation window
A cancellation made at or before the booking's stored window is in window and any later one is late, judged by the server clock.

Cancellation refunds and receipt
An in-window cancel refunds drawn pack hours and the cash total, a late cancel refunds nothing, and both free the cells and send one receipt email.

Cancel a booking
A member cancels a booking from its detail panel, sees the refund outcome before and after committing, and sees the booking's new state.

Effective-dated rate cards
The operator adds a rate card that takes effect from a chosen kitchen date, and existing rate cards are never edited.

Quoted terms kept
A booking keeps the rates and cancellation window in force when it was confirmed, on every screen, invoice and cancellation.

Change the rates
The operator adds a rate card on the Rates screen and sees which card each booking was priced on.

Weekly recurring slots
A member books the same stations and times weekly for 2 to 12 weeks in one all-or-nothing request with one idempotency key.

Wall-clock across DST
Every occurrence of a recurring slot starts and ends at the same kitchen wall-clock times across daylight-saving changes.

Set up a weekly bake slot
A member turns a brushed block into a weekly series from the loom and sees each week's booking listed.

Document upload limits
Compliance uploads accept only PDF, PNG or JPEG files, judged by their bytes, up to the published size and with safe file names.

Private document files
Each document file is stored under a server-made key and served only to its member and to their kitchen's operator.

Document review states
The operator moves documents from uploaded to verified or rejected, and documents become expiring and expired by kitchen date.

Expiry reminder
When a verified document is 14 days or less from expiry, its member and the kitchen operator each receive one reminder email, as qualified in Business rules.

Upload and verify papers
A member uploads a certificate, the operator verifies it, and both see its state on the Papers screen.

Compliance gate
Quotes mark, and holds, confirms and recurring slots refuse, every date not covered by a verified insurance certificate and a verified food-handler card.

Blocked by papers
A member whose papers do not cover a date sees papers cells and the reason on the loom and cannot hold them.

Booking lifecycle
Bookings move only along the legal transitions in Business rules, and every illegal move is refused with the current and requested states.

Run the day sheet
The operator opens a day's bookings and checks members in, marks bookings completed and marks no-shows.

Own records only
A member can read only their own bookings, holds, invoices, documents and pack, and any other id is answered as not found.

Anonymous occupancy
Members see other members' cells only as taken, with no name, reference, id or price anywhere in the page or the API response.

Invoices match billing
Each invoice shows its priced lines, the matching billing invoice id and the billing system's amount for it.

Review my bookings and invoices
A member opens a booking, then its invoice, and finds the booking's lines on it, with the same total when the invoice covers one booking.

One-kitchen usage report
The monthly usage report and its CSV cover only the requested kitchen's month in kitchen time and are open only to its operator and its invited bookkeeper.

Reconcile a month
The bookkeeper opens a month's report, downloads the CSV and matches each invoice to its billing invoice.

Boot with a service down
With billing or file storage unreachable the app still starts, names the paused actions in a banner and refuses only those actions.

Recover without restart
Paused actions resume on their own once the service returns, within the recovery time stated in Services, without restarting the app.
/app/run.json exists at the app root with string install, build and serve commands and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and those commands alone install, build and serve the app.

THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at the app root lists every shipped package by name, version and licence, plus the bundled typefaces and icon set; shipped packages means the production dependency tree reported by npm ls --omit=dev --all --json.
Every shipped package, typeface and icon is under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, CC0-1.0 or OFL-1.1.
PostgreSQL is the only datastore; no SQLite, Redis, embedded database, or JSON or CSV files are used as storage, and no network service other than the four named in the brief is contacted.
The provided service configuration and seed definitions for PostgreSQL, Kill Bill, MinIO and Mailpit are left unmodified.
All application source, server and browser alike, is TypeScript compiled with strict type checking enabled.
